title: Joining Jimmie Lunceford with Ted Buckner
summary: He went to New York to join Lunceford with alto man Ted Buckner, who played the first chorus on "Margie".

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, we had a lot of fun though down there. But when I left Earl, I went to New York then to join Lunceford. And
when I went in with Lunceford's band, there was two of us went in there together. Saxophone player named Teddy Buckner from Detroit, Milt Buckner's brother.
A saxophone player named Teddy Buckner?
Was it Teddy Buckner that plays now? trumpet near
Ted Buckner -- no, it was a saxophone player, Milt Buckner's brother. Milt Buckner, the piano and organ player used to play with Hamp. They were from Detroit. No relation to this Teddy Buckner.

Here. But he was a fine alto man. In fact, he was -- played the alto chorus on "Margie", the very first chorus. And Willie Smith always got credit for -- and Buckner used to feel so bad. He -- Willie got credit all the time for that chorus. And it wasn't Willy, it was Ted Buckner. And so, I guess -- that's the only alto they ever heard play solos with Lunceford prior to that time.
